title: Cough
hpi_narrative: {{patient_name}} presents with acute productive cough, fever, dyspnea, and pleuritic chest pain. Exam reveals crackles and bronchial breath sounds over the affected lobe. CXR shows lobar consolidation. CAP severity assessed by CURB-65 or PORT score to determine outpatient vs inpatient treatment. Most common pathogens: S. pneumoniae (most common), H. influenzae, M. catarrhalis, atypical bacteria (Mycoplasma, Chlamydia, Legionella). Outpatient treatment (no comorbidities): amoxicillin or doxycycline or macrolide (azithromycin). Outpatient with comorbidities: respiratory fluoroquinolone (levofloxacin) or beta-lactam + macrolide. Inpatient non-ICU: beta-lactam (ceftriaxone) + macrolide. Inpatient ICU: beta-lactam + macrolide OR beta-lactam + fluoroquinolone. Add vancomycin if MRSA risk. Blood cultures and sputum cultures BEFORE antibiotics if inpatient. Smoking cessation counseling. Pneumococcal vaccine if indicated.
